verdict.rationale: The only first-party evidence of no-cost use is the browser MCP Inspector, documented as usable with "No login required." That lets a developer test and prototype tool connections without paying, but no documented free plan or limits appear. A community report adds that a credit card was required, without documentation, for rebuild/release on hosted servers, which limits how far free prototyping goes. Missing for 10: an explicitly documented free tier with stated limits, free hosting/gateway usage for prototyping, independent confirmation of a meaningful free allowance.

support.subject: As a developer, I can prototype my agent's tool connections on a meaningful free tier before paying anything

citations.quote: Inspect any MCP server directly from your browser. No login required.
Test any MCP server from your browser. Supports every Model Context Protocol feature, including tools, resources, prompts, tasks, elicitation, sampling, and OAuth 2.1.
Turned out a credit card was required for rebuild/release to work, which wasn't documented
